nodes.speaker: CHR-17
nodes.text: Trefan! Heel! - Sorry, mister. Dog's got no manners and I've got no say over him. He's been odd all week, anyway. Odd near the mill, special.

choices.text: Odd near the mill? How do you mean?
Steady, Ifor. Breathe. Now - where, exactly?
I should get to the mill myself, before the path is all boots.
Keep hold of him. Good dog, Trefan.

nodes.speaker: CHR-17
nodes.text: Growls at the wheel-race like there's something IN the water, mister. Won't drink below the sluice, and that's a dog that'd drink out of a boot. Mam says dogs are daft. Dogs aren't daft. Daft things don't live as long as dogs do.

nodes.speaker: CHR-17
nodes.text: It's the mill, mister! They've stopped the wheel - Father's gone ahead with the lantern, and there's folk gathering on the path, and they're saying - they're saying Nott's dead in his own flour. Mouth full of salt, they're saying. Will you come? They let grown men nearer than boys. I could hold the lantern. I hold it fine.

nodes.speaker: CHR-17
nodes.text: Trefan's already pulling toward the bridge. The boy follows the dog, and the dog, it seems, has already decided where everyone is meant to be this morning.
